biography.plain_text: Alexander Girda is a Russian entrepreneur who co-founded the Pyatyorochka discount grocery chain and the Karusel hypermarket business. An engineering graduate of Riga’s civil aviation institute, he built his fortune in food retailing. Pyatyorochka’s merger with Perekrestok created X5 Retail Group, in which Girda and his fellow founders retained a substantial shareholding.

confidence.reason: Primary company history and the dedicated Forbes profile support the historical identity and mechanism.

long_biography.plain_text:
A warehouse problem helped turn Alexander Girda from a food wholesaler into a retailer. His imported dairy business joined Andrei Rogachev’s canned-food operation shortly before the Russian financial crisis of 1998. When imported goods stopped selling, the partners opened their own shops to clear the stock. The first Pyatyorochka outlets followed.

Girda also became a film producer, backing The Strawberries Time and Yuri Mamin’s Don’t Think About White Monkeys. For Mamin’s film, he shared producing duties with Lyudmila Samokhvalova. The tragicomedy used dialogue in verse and won a Russian film-critics’ award, as well as a prize at the Smile, Russia! festival.

confidence.reason: Business newspaper’s full account and complete trade-film report support distinct commercial circumstances and credited creative work.
